meta.title: Dry Blood
meta.source_file: Dry Blood By Parallels (Official Music Video).mp3

interpretation.summary: A driving, powerful, and bright acoustic-style drum performance with a strong 4/4 rock backbeat, characterized by a punchy kick, a sharp reverberant snare, and constant, crisp hi-hats.

vocabulary.timbre: The timbre is predominantly percussive and noisy, characteristic of a full drum kit. The kick provides a low thud, the snare a sharp, filtered noise crack, and the cymbals a bright, metallic shimmer. Though based on acoustic drum sounds, the punch and clarity suggest studio processing and perhaps layered electronic sources.
vocabulary.brightness: Extremely bright, with a high spectral centroid (mean 6485 Hz). This is driven by the constant presence of crisp, metallic hi-hats and shimmering crash/ride cymbals that dominate the high-frequency spectrum. The snare also has a significant high-end snap.
vocabulary.envelope: The envelopes are sharp and percussive across the board. All instruments feature a nearly instantaneous attack. The kick and closed hi-hats have very short decays, creating a tight groove, while the snare has a slightly longer decay due to reverb, and crash cymbals have a long, natural release.
vocabulary.register_density: The track occupies the full frequency spectrum, from the low-end kick (<100Hz) to the high-frequency sizzle of cymbals (>10kHz). The rhythmic density is high, built on a constant 8th-note hi-hat pattern. Density increases significantly during fills and cymbal-heavy choruses.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: Atonal and percussive. The track consists entirely of unpitched percussion instruments. The provided key of C# minor is not expressed by the drum parts.
vocabulary.groove: A driving, straight-ahead 4/4 rock groove at 120 BPM. The foundation is a strong kick on the downbeats and a powerful snare backbeat on beats 2 and 4. Continuous 8th-note hi-hats provide forward momentum, with syncopated fills adding variation.
vocabulary.space_grit: The sound is polished and powerful, with a distinct sense of space created by a noticeable hall or plate reverb, especially on the snare. There's little overt distortion or 'grit', but a high degree of compression and saturation adds punch and weight, giving the kit a larger-than-life feel.

tracks.name: Power Kick
tracks.pattern: A foundational rock pattern, primarily landing on beats 1 and 3, with occasional syncopated 8th notes to add drive.
tracks.description: The low-end anchor of the entire track. It provides a consistent, punchy pulse that is present through almost the entire duration.

tracks.name: Backbeat Snare
tracks.pattern: A solid, unwavering backbeat on 2 and 4, occasionally embellished with ghost notes and leading into fills.
tracks.description: The defining element of the groove, providing a sharp, cracking sound with noticeable reverb that gives it size. It cuts through the mix clearly.

tracks.name: Driving Hats
tracks.pattern: Constant, driving 8th notes, with accents created by velocity variation and periodic open-hat sizzles on an off-beat.
tracks.description: The main time-keeping element, providing high-frequency energy and a sense of constant motion. The sound is tight and metallic.

tracks.name: Crash Cymbals
tracks.pattern: Dramatic, explosive accents landing on the downbeat of major phrases (e.g., beat 1 of an 8-bar section).
tracks.description: Used for emphasis and to mark structural transitions. The crashes are bright, loud, and have a long, shimmering decay, adding a sense of scale and drama.

tracks.name: Tom Fills
tracks.pattern: Fast 16th-note runs, typically over one or two beats, used to connect phrases and build tension.
tracks.description: These fills provide rhythmic variation and excitement, usually appearing at the end of a 4 or 8 bar phrase before a chorus or new section. They are tuned from high to low.

interpretation.score_draft: SPECULATIVE STARTER: This is a classic rock drum pattern. Use Tone.Part to sequence these components. The core groove is Kick, Snare, and Hats. Kick: `MembraneSynth({ pitchDecay: 0.05, attack: 0.001, decay: 0.1, volume: -4 })`. Snare: `NoiseSynth({ noise: {type: 'pink'}, envelope: { decay: 0.2 }, volume: -8 })` through a `bandpass` filter around 3-4kHz and a `Reverb` with a 1.5s decay and 0.4 wet mix. Hats/Cymbals: `MetalSynth` is ideal. For closed hats, use very short `decay` (0.05). For crashes, use a long `release` (3.0+). Tom fills can be done with multiple `MembraneSynth` instances at different pitches (e.g., C2, G2, A2). A driving 8th-note hi-hat loop: `['x','x','x','x','x','x','x','x']`. A standard beat: Kick: `['C1', null, null, null, 'C1', null, 'C1', null]`, Snare: `[null, null, 'x', null, null, null, 'x', null]`. Use compression on the master bus to glue it all together and add punch.

interpretation.summary: A heavily processed female lead vocal accompanied by multiple layers of harmony and a massive reverb. The track consists entirely of sung lyrical phrases and occasional breathy textures, creating an ethereal and atmospheric soundscape. The arrangement builds from a single voice to a dense, choral wall of sound in the choruses.

vocabulary.timbre: The timbre is that of a layered, processed human female voice. It's fundamentally tonal and smooth, but the stacking of multiple takes and harmonies creates a rich, choral texture akin to a synth's unison detuning. The high harmonic ratio confirms its tonal, non-percussive nature.
vocabulary.brightness: Moderately bright and airy, with a mean spectral centroid of 1975 Hz. The sound has significant high-frequency content from breath and reverb shimmer, but the fundamental vocal tone is smooth and rounded, with a spectral rolloff at 3280 Hz preventing harshness.
vocabulary.envelope: The envelope follows natural vocal phrasing, with soft attacks, sustained notes determined by the singer, and long, gradual releases artificially extended by a very large, washed-out reverb. Dynamics are expressive, swelling into choruses and receding for verses.
vocabulary.register_density: The lead vocal is in the female alto to mezzo-soprano range. The density is dynamic, starting with a single vocal line and building to a very high density in the choruses, where multiple harmony parts are layered to create thick, resonant chords.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: The harmony is firmly in E minor, creating a melancholic and spacious atmosphere. Vocal harmonies are stacked in diatonic thirds, fourths, and fifths, often creating dense, lush chordal textures that support the lead melody.
vocabulary.groove: The groove is fluid and lyrical, dictated by the sung phrases rather than a strict metronome. The rhythm floats around the beat, with long, legato phrases punctuated by more rhythmically defined, syncopated lines in the pre-chorus sections.
vocabulary.space_grit: The space is immense and defining. A cavernous reverb with a very long decay time and high wet/dry mix envelops the vocals, making them sound distant and ethereal. There is very little grit or distortion; the sound is overwhelmingly clean, smooth, and washed-out.

tracks.name: Ethereal Lead Vocals
tracks.pattern: Melodic, lyrical phrases that follow the song's structure. Verses are sparser, while choruses feature dense, multi-part harmonies. The rhythm is largely based on quarter and eighth notes with significant legato and long-held notes, all saturated in reverb.
tracks.description: This single track represents the entire vocal arrangement, including the lead, doubles, and harmony layers. It is the sole melodic and harmonic element in this stem, present from the beginning to the end. The defining characteristic is the massive reverb wash that glues all vocal layers together into a single atmospheric entity.

interpretation.score_draft: SPECULATIVE STARTER: The core sound can be approximated with a Tone.js PolySynth. For the oscillator, use a 'fatsawtooth' with a count of 5 and spread of 30 to mimic layered voices. Set a soft attack (~0.1s), high sustain (1.0), and a long release (~1.2s) to allow notes to bleed. Add a lowpass filter around 3300Hz with a Q of 2 for shape. The most critical effect is a very large reverb; connect the synth to a Convolver or Reverb with a long decay time and set the synth's reverbSend to 0.8 or higher. Add a touch of Chorus (~0.4) for extra width. The melody is in E minor. Create patterns on a '16n' grid, using multi-note strings like 'E4+G4+B4' to simulate harmonies and empty strings for rests to create lyrical, flowing phrases.

interpretation.summary: A dense, driving synth-wave arrangement featuring a prominent 16th-note arpeggio, a soaring, atmospheric lead/pad, and a gritty, supportive bass arpeggio. The piece is built on classic synth-pop textures with heavy use of reverb and chorus to create a large, immersive soundscape.

vocabulary.timbre: Dominated by synthesized, tonal sounds. A mix of plucky, short-decay arpeggios and sustained, wide pads with detuned sawtooth waveforms. Mild drive on the lower layer adds warmth.
vocabulary.brightness: Moderately bright, with a constant high-mid energy from the arpeggios, consistent with the 2442 Hz spectral centroid. The sound is open and clear, shaped by high-set low-pass filters.
vocabulary.envelope: A duality of envelopes defines the texture: a very short, plucky envelope (fast attack/decay, low sustain) for the arpeggios, contrasted with a slow-swelling envelope (slow attack, long release) for the lead pads.
vocabulary.register_density: The texture is dense and wide-ranging. A continuous stream of 16th-note arpeggios fills the mid-range (C4-A5), anchored by a low-mid bass layer (A2-E3) and topped by high-register pads (E5+).
vocabulary.harmony_mode: Firmly in A minor, using diatonic chord progressions typical of the synth-wave genre (e.g., Am-G-C-F). Both arpeggios and lead lines adhere strictly to the A natural minor scale.
vocabulary.groove: The groove is relentless and machine-like, driven by a straight 16th-note grid from the arpeggios. There is no swing; the feel is purely metric, with sustained pads floating over the rigid rhythmic base.
vocabulary.space_grit: The production employs a large, cavernous space, with significant reverb applied to all layers. The lead pad has an especially wide stereo image from a prominent chorus effect. Grit is minimal, limited to light saturation on the bass layer.

tracks.name: Classic Arp
tracks.pattern: Continuous 16th-note arpeggio outlining transposed chord progressions. The pattern is a fast, multi-octave figure that forms the primary rhythmic and melodic element.
tracks.description: The main rhythmic and harmonic driver of the track, present from the beginning. It has a bright, plucky sound with a significant amount of reverb, creating a wash of notes that propels the song forward.

tracks.name: Soaring Lead Pad
tracks.pattern: Long, sustained notes and simple, evolving melodic lines. Notes often hold for one or more bars, creating a slow-moving harmonic layer.
tracks.description: Enters at 0:33 to provide an epic, atmospheric layer. Sits high in the mix with a very wide stereo field (from chorus) and a long reverb tail. Its slow attack allows it to swell in and out of the arrangement.

tracks.name: Gritty Bass Arp
tracks.pattern: Plays a simplified 16th-note arpeggio in the low-mid register, often outlining the root and fifth of the current chord.
tracks.description: Adds rhythmic weight and a touch of aggression to the low-mids, entering around 0:33. This is a synth bass line with mild drive that locks in with the main arp, rather than a sub-bass.

interpretation.summary: A driving, repetitive synth bass line plays a constant 8th-note pattern, forming the rhythmic and harmonic foundation of the track with a gritty, filtered tone.

vocabulary.timbre: A tonal, synthetic bass sound, characteristic of a filtered sawtooth wave with unison detuning for thickness and subtle overdrive for grit.
vocabulary.brightness: Dark but defined, occupying the low-mid frequency range (mean centroid 426 Hz). The lowpass filter keeps it from being harsh, but allows enough upper harmonics to cut through.
vocabulary.envelope: A quick attack creates a distinct pluck on each note, followed by a quick decay to a high sustain level, resulting in a continuous but articulated 'pushed' feel.
vocabulary.register_density: A single, dense monophonic line plays a continuous stream of 8th notes, primarily in a low register (A1-A2) with occasional octave jumps for variation.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: Rooted firmly in A minor, the bassline outlines the chord progression by playing the root notes in a driving, modal fashion.
vocabulary.groove: A straight, machine-like 1/8th note pulse at 120 BPM provides the track's relentless and hypnotic rhythmic drive.
vocabulary.space_grit: The sound is direct, present, and gritty due to saturation or drive. There are minimal spatial effects like reverb or delay, keeping the bassline focused and in the forefront.

tracks.name: Driving Mid-Bass
tracks.pattern: A relentless 8th-note pattern outlining chord roots, typically in a repeating 2-bar or 4-bar phrase. The filter cutoff subtly opens in more intense sections.
tracks.description: The core rhythmic and harmonic engine, present from the start and playing nearly continuously. It provides a constant, hypnotic pulse that underpins the entire song.

overview.summary: A driving, anthemic 80s-inspired synth-pop track at 120 BPM in A minor. It features a classic four-on-the-floor drum machine beat, a propulsive 16th-note arpeggiated bassline, gated chords, and a soaring lead synth melody. The production uses heavy gated reverb to create a large, cavernous soundscape, while the core instrumental elements remain punchy and defined.

vocabulary.timbre: A classic retro-analog synthesis palette, blending bright, cutting sawtooth and square leads with thick, chorused pads and a punchy, filtered bass. Percussion is based on classic drum machine sounds with significant noise components and reverb.
vocabulary.brightness: Crisp and bright, with a high spectral centroid. Shimmering hi-hats and cutting lead synths occupy the high frequencies, balanced by a powerful mid-range from chords and a focused low-end from the bass and kick.
vocabulary.envelope: Predominantly plucky and gated. Basslines and rhythmic chords have very fast attacks and short, abrupt decays creating a tight, percussive feel. This contrasts with soaring lead lines and background pads which use longer attacks and releases.
vocabulary.register_density: Layered and wide-ranging. The arrangement builds from a sparse intro to a dense, full-spectrum texture. It utilizes deep sub-bass, a busy mid-range with arpeggios and chords, and high-frequency lead melodies and percussion.
vocabulary.harmony_mode: Driving minor key. The harmony is firmly rooted in A minor, using simple, powerful chord progressions (i-VII-VI) typical of the 80s pop/rock style, reinforcing a feeling of moody determination.
vocabulary.groove: Four-on-the-floor. A straight, propulsive 4/4 groove is established by the kick drum, with a strong backbeat from a prominent gated snare. The constant 16th-note bass arpeggio provides relentless rhythmic energy.
vocabulary.space_grit: Cavernous and saturated. The mix is defined by a large, ambient space created with heavy use of reverb, especially a gated effect on the snare. Synths have a light to moderate analog-style saturation (drive) for warmth and presence, without being overtly distorted.

tracks.name: Kick Drum
tracks.pattern: A driving four-on-the-floor pattern, hitting every quarter note.
tracks.description: The foundational pulse of the track. A punchy, medium-weight kick sound that provides constant energy. Enters at the start of the first beat drop and continues throughout.

tracks.name: Gated Snare
tracks.pattern: A strong backbeat on counts 2 and 4.
tracks.description: A classic 80s snare sound with a burst of noise and a huge, gated reverb tail. This defines the spacious character of the drum groove.

tracks.name: Sixteenth Hats
tracks.pattern: Continuous 16th notes with a slight accent pattern.
tracks.description: Crisp, metallic 16th-note hi-hats that provide a top-end shimmer and enhance the rhythmic drive. Present through most of the track.

tracks.name: Arpeggio Bass
tracks.pattern: A constant, sequenced 16th-note arpeggio outlining the chord progression.
tracks.description: The primary rhythmic and harmonic driving force of the song. A tight, focused sawtooth bass sound with a resonant filter that plays a relentless arpeggio. Enters after the intro and is a core element.

tracks.name: Stab Chords
tracks.pattern: Gated, punchy power chords playing a rhythmic pattern.
tracks.description: A thick, detuned synth playing short, staccato chords that punctuate the rhythm, often in conversation with the main melody. A key textural element that adds to the 80s character.

tracks.name: Soaring Lead
tracks.pattern: A memorable, singable melodic line with held notes and expressive phrasing.
tracks.description: The main melodic voice of the track. A bright, powerful, and slightly detuned lead sound with significant chorus and reverb. Carries the main theme during the chorus sections.

tracks.name: Atmosphere Pad
tracks.pattern: Sustained, whole-note chords that follow the main progression.
tracks.description: A dark, low-mid pad with a slow attack and long release. It fills out the harmonic space in the background, providing a bed for the other elements without drawing attention.

overview.score_draft: SPECULATIVE STARTER: To approximate 'Dry Blood', set tempo to 120 BPM in A minor. Use a `MembraneSynth` for the kick in a 4/4 pattern: `['C1', 'C1', 'C1', 'C1']`. The snare is a `NoiseSynth` with a short decay and heavy reverb on beats 2 and 4. The main engine is a `MonoSynth` (`oscillatorType: 'sawtooth'`) with a low-pass filter (cutoff ~800Hz, Q ~2) playing a 16th-note arpeggio like `['A2', 'E3', 'A3', 'E3', ...]`. Layer this with a `PolySynth` (`oscillatorType: 'fatsquare'`) playing gated power chords like `['A3+E4', '', 'G3+D4', '']`. The lead melody can be a `MonoSynth` with `oscillatorType: 'fatsawtooth'`, chorus, and reverb, playing a simple line in A minor. Background pads are a `PolySynth` with a very slow attack (`>1.5s`), long release, and high chorus, holding chords like 'Am' and 'G'.
